title: Neko Atsume: Kitty Collector
lede: Hit-Point’s mobile game in which round, simply drawn cats visit a yard; its interface uses thick outlines, rounded panels, and paw-print motifs.
summary: Cat-collecting mobile game with outlined cats, rounded cream panels, and a paw-print menu button. Hit-Point, 2014.

source.label: App Store: Neko Atsume: Kitty Collector

evidence.note: Inspected three App Store screenshots of the current English iOS version (1000 px wide, scratchpad copies): the yard view and the shop. The screenshots may differ from the 2014 release. Not stored.

styles.note: Partial fit: dot-eyed cats, rounded outlined panels, and paw motifs are kawaii interface grammar, but the palette is muted earth and green rather than pastel.

context: Wikipedia describes Neko Atsume as a cat-collecting game for iOS and Android by Hit-Point, released on 20 October 2014; players set out food, toys, and furniture to attract cats, then take photos and receive gifts of dried sardines. It won the CEDEC Award for game design in August 2015. [Wikipedia: Neko Atsume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neko_Atsume).
observed: The yard is drawn in flat fills with an even dark-brown outline: a green hedge, a red-roofed house, a tree stump, a tatami mat, and a cardboard box.
Cats are short, round bodies with small round heads, two dot eyes, and a tiny “ω” mouth; one hugs a ball, one lies on a stump.
The menu button is a rounded square in orange with a white paw print and the word “Menu” in a rounded hand-drawn face.
In the shop, items sit in cream cards with thick dark outlines and very round corners, on a mint-green ground patterned with faint paw prints.
A pill-shaped speech bubble reads “Gifts Await”; prices use bold rounded numerals next to small fish icons.
interpretation: The game applies kawaii to a whole interface: the characters set the mood, and the controls are drawn in the same outlined, rounded hand. The cats are decorative and never carry information, which matches the style’s rules.
The muted, domestic palette is a quieter branch of the style; it relies on line and shape more than on pastel color.
borrow: Draw interface cards and buttons with the same thick outline as the characters, so the whole screen feels like one sticker sheet.
Use a faint repeated motif (paw prints) as a low-contrast background pattern.
